method: The list is ISO 3166-1 as the iso-codes data set publishes it: 249 officially assigned entries, each with a two-letter alpha-2, a three-letter alpha-3, a three-digit numeric code that keeps its leading zeros, the English short name, the official name where ISO publishes one, the ISO common name where one exists, and the fuller name some tables print. The input is split on newlines, commas and semicolons and each entry is resolved on its own. A token of one to three digits is read as a numeric code, zero-padded to three places, so 4 and 004 both find Afghanistan; a two-letter token is read as alpha-2 and a three-letter token as alpha-3, either case, before any name is considered, which is why and returns Andorra. Everything else is folded to lower case with accents, punctuation and repeated spaces removed and matched against the short, official, common and alternate names, with the ISO inverted names ("Korea, Republic of") also matched the other way round ("Republic of Korea"): an exact match first, then a name that starts with the query, then a name that contains it. A stage that matches one entry resolves it, a stage that matches several is reported as ambiguous with up to four of the candidates named, and a query that matches nothing is reported as not found rather than guessed. Sixteen everyday names that ISO does not use are mapped explicitly, among them Britain and UK to GB, Holland to NL, Turkey to TR, Russia to RU, Ivory Coast to CI, Burma to MM, Swaziland to SZ, Cape Verde to CV and the UAE to AE. Up to 50 entries are converted at a time; an empty input and a longer list are refused. The tool is a reference lookup, not an authority: it prints the codes ISO assigns and never derives one. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: IBAN.com - "Country Codes": the ISO 3166-1 table of country names with the alpha-2, alpha-3 and three-digit numeric codes, including the leading zeros (Afghanistan 004, Andorra 020, Austria 040) and the same 249 entries this list holds

iso-codes - ISO 3166-1 data (JSON): the machine-readable copy of the code list that supplies each alpha-2, alpha-3, numeric code, English short name, official name and ISO common name used here, including Cote d'Ivoire, Turkiye, Eswatini and the common names South Korea, Vietnam and Taiwan
